column1: # Known slow calls: our per-call cost against Metal's, where it is over an order of magnitude.
# READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A ROW. A row here is not an accepted difference and it is not permission
# for anything. It is a call that costs an order of magnitude more than Metal's over the cases both
# legs did exactly, written down so the one call that holds an open bug visible does not make every
# run red and teach everyone to stop reading the report. Nothing here is resolved by being listed.
# The gate is held in BOTH directions (src/slow_calls.rs): a call over the margin that is not
# listed fails the run, and a listed call that has come back inside the band fails it too, saying
# the row looks fixed and must go. So a row cannot outlive the bug it stands for.
# There is a third state, and it fails nothing: a row the measurement cannot resolve, or a whole
# measurement whose own instrument says it was taken on a CPU the figures cannot be compared across,
# is WITHHELD. Withholding neither adds a row nor retires one, and the run says which rows and why.
# Before adding a row, LOCALISE IT: `conformance times --runs 8 --call <name>` prints the call case
# by case. A per-call total says that a call is expensive and never where, and the first row below
# was 105x over the whole set and 1.2x over the three cases that obviously make it.
# AND THEN READ THE PER-CASE TOTAL BESIDE IT, WHICH IS THE CHECK THIS FILE WAS MISSING. Metal
# compiles the AIR at `MTLLibrary` creation and we translate it at pipeline creation and at
# reflection, so the same work sits at a DIFFERENT CALL on each leg -- README.md says so and says
# "neither row alone is a result", and five rows were nevertheless written here off the per-call
# figure alone. Measured over the stored 19:57 pass, per case, our leg against Metal's:
#   function-facts-*                 0.04x   (Metal 343 ms, ours 13 ms over 15 cases)
#   library-facts-descriptor-*       0.02x   (Metal 156 ms, ours 3.8 ms over 7)
#   function-bindings-*              0.15x   (Metal 320 ms, ours 49 ms over 13)
#   attribute-stride-*               0.07x
#   mesh-pipeline-reflection-*       0.43x
#   blend-sweep-*                    0.68x, with two cases at 1.25x and 1.55x
#   attribute-format-*               1.92x, with attribute-format-fetches at 2.68x
#   xr-two-plane*                    0.23x  -- and replace_region's row is a REAL bug
# Metal pays 21-27 ms at `library` in every one of those cases and we pay 0.05-0.8 ms. So a call
# that reads 20x or 50x against Metal while its CASE reads 0.04x is not a cost finding at all; it
# is the placement of the compile, and a row that quotes only the per-call ratio tells a reader we
# are slow where we are 25 times faster.
# AND HERE IS WHAT THE PER-CASE FIGURES ACTUALLY SAY, which is the one finding in this cluster
# worth acting on. Sort every paired case by how many pipelines it creates on our leg:
#   pipelines a case creates    cases    median case ratio, ours over Metal
#   21 or more                    10     2.49x
# Metal compiles a library eagerly and we translate a variant when a pipeline needs it, so while a
# case makes few pipelines Metal's eager compile is largely wasted and we win by 4x to 14x. The
# advantage is spent by about twenty pipelines and REVERSES past that, because our per-pipeline
# translation is dear where Metal's marginal pipeline is cheap. The ten cases past the turn, worst
# first: integer-vertex-attributes 3.62x (64 pipelines, Metal 37.8 ms against our 136.8 ms),
# vertex-format-constant-step 3.08x, attribute-format-fetches 2.68x, vertex-format-half4 2.60x,
# vertex-format-float4 2.52x, vertex-format-instance-step 2.46x, blend-sweep-write-masks 1.55x,
# blend-sweep-operations 1.25x, blend-interaction-mask-blend 1.05x, blend-sweep-operation-pairs
# So the cost this round was sent to find is REAL and it is none of the ten calls it named: it is
# the per-pipeline translation, it is visible only on the cases that create many pipelines, and at
# 3.62x worst it is under the per-case margin of 10x, so the suite's per-case verdict reads
# `within` on every one of them. Neither half of this instrument sees it today. A per-call row
# cannot carry it, and nothing below should be mistaken for it.
# WHAT STILL DESERVES A ROW, then. The per-call gate is right to exist -- replace_region is 265x
# with 92% of ours blocked, the caller waiting 1.1 ms where Metal writes through in 4 us, and its
# case total is 0.23x, so NOTHING BUT a per-call gate could ever have seen it. What distinguishes
# it is not the size of the ratio: it is that the cost is work Metal does not do at all (a wait),
# rather than work Metal already did earlier in the case. So before writing a row, answer which of
# the two it is, and put the per-case figure in the row either way.
# A ratio here is a measurement and it moves MORE THAN EITHER OF ITS HALVES, because the two halves
# move independently. THREE independent whole-set passes have now been recorded on this M3 Max, and
# every figure below is from their stored per-case records (`times --write` keeps both legs in each
# case's recording, so a pass can be re-read without re-running it). They are not equal in quality:
#   pass    instrument (metal/ours)   load (metal/ours)   paired cases
# The 07:44 pass is the degraded one, and the instrument says so: it cost 0.275 us a call against
# 0.236 us in the quietest pass, and its figures are not reproducible by the binary that produced
# them -- re-run over the same fifteen cases, that binary reads function_facts at 46.3x and 40.9x
# against the 89.5x it recorded, and its per-case figures agree with the later passes' to within 5%.
# The cause is the CPU the measurement ran on, not the call: one binary and one case set inside one
# minute read 38.8x at the ordinary scheduling class and 75.5x under a background one, while the
# one-minute load average held at 6.1.
# WHAT THE THIRD PASS CHANGES. The movement this file's band was set from is almost entirely that
# one pass. Over the paired rows common to each pair:
# and restricted to the rows both passes resolve above the instrument (RESOLVES_AT), 1.87x / 6.92x,
# 1.58x / 4.96x, and 1.10x / 1.51x / worst 1.97x. The first line is the pair this file's band was
# set from, and reading it back out of the stored recordings reproduces its published figures to
# the digit, which is what says the other two lines are measured the same way. (The three passes
# ran over 1031, 1084 and 1099 cases as the suite grew, so a pair's rows are its common ones; the
# 98-row comparison the band was set from has the same property, and 15 cases of 1084 is 1.4%.)
# BETWEEN TWO UNDEGRADED PASSES THE WORST MOVEMENT OVER ALL 100 ROWS IS 2.00x -- below even the
# 2.43x the original margin / 2.5 divisor was set from. So the ratio is not inherently unstable;
# a degraded CPU is what makes it look that way, and `band` being margin / 7.0 rather than margin / 2.5 is paying for a pass the
# gate should have refused. It did not refuse it: 0.275 against 0.236 us is 1.17x, under the 1.5x
# CALIBRATION_MAY_MOVE allows, so the calibration reference check passed a pass whose figures move
# 64x. Tightening that check is the fix, and it is the owner's call, not this file's.
# WHAT THAT MEANS FOR A ROW, CORRECTED. This header used to say that six calls "read far over the
# margin in one of those two passes and far under it in the other", and name
# texture_accesses, function_facts, function_facts_from_descriptor, mesh_pipeline_bindings,
# compute_pipeline_with_stage_input and compute_pipeline_bindings. THAT WAS WRONG, and it is why
# nobody localised them: of those six, only compute_pipeline_bindings actually crossed the margin
# (7.5x then 21.7x and 23.6x -- and the pass that read it UNDER the margin is the degraded one).
# 40.6x, 28.5x, 18.5x and 22.6x are not "far under" an order of magnitude; they are over it, in both
# undegraded passes. The sentence confused a ratio MOVING a lot with a ratio CHANGING SIDES, and on
# that confusion four live per-call costs went unwritten. The calls the degraded pass really did
# invent, each over the margin at 07:44 and comfortably within the band in both undegraded passes,
# are these, and none of them has or needs a row: argument_encoder 36.4x then 4.1x and 3.9x,
# copy_rate_map_parameters 29.9x then 0.5x and 0.5x (we are twice as fast as Metal), dispatch 17.9x
# then 4.4x and 4.0x, compute_pipeline 14.8x then 4.3x and 4.7x, and compute_pipeline_for_commands
# 27.2x then 5.1x and 5.5x.
# WHAT BECAME OF THE FOUR, and the per-case check above is what decided it. mesh_pipeline_bindings
# (0.43x a case), compute_pipeline_bindings (0.15x) and compute_pipeline_with_stage_input's
# attribute-stride half (0.07x) are the compile's placement and not a cost: they keep rows only
# because the gate is per call, and each row says so in its first words. The one family whose case
# total goes the wrong way is attribute-format-*, 1.92x and 2.68x on attribute-format-fetches, and
# that is the single genuine per-case cost this whole cluster contains. function_facts and function_facts_from_descriptor have rows too, and
# they also have a FIX, because their cause was structural rather than a timing: both answer
# through the suite's own
# our_function_facts, which reads five MTLFunction property getters, and every one of the five
# recomputed the function's properties from scratch -- a full AIR decode each, for a module-sourced
# function -- so one reflection call decoded one function's AIR five times over, six with the
# constants dictionary, and ten for a specialized function, which decodes again to specialize. The
# stored pass says so without a timing: the one case of the family whose function needs no decode,
# function-facts-visible, is the one case we are FASTER than Metal on (0.2x) while its fourteen
# siblings run 19.0x to 101.6x, every microsecond of it the caller's own CPU with nothing blocked.
# The runtime now memoizes a function's properties as Metal's MTLFunction already holds them
# (metal2vulkan-runtime/src/library.rs), and the redundancy is held by a count rather than a time
# (metal2vulkan-runtime tests::derived_once: reading the getters derives the properties
# once; with the memo bypassed the same test reads ten). BOTH KEEP A ROW BELOW ANYWAY, with the
# figure the stored pass read, because the gate is per call and an unlisted over-margin row fails
# the run. NO ROW HERE QUOTES AN EXPECTED RATIO. What the memo is proven by is the count, which is
# deterministic and needed no quiet host; the ratio was never the cost, as the per-case figures
# say, and an expectation in place of a measurement is the thing this file keeps having to correct.
# Whoever re-measures replaces the per-call figure with what they read and leaves the per-case
# line, which is the half that decides whether anything is wrong.
# texture_accesses is a third thing again, and the gate has it right: 19.3x, 102.4x, 158.5x, on five
# calls whose cheaper leg is a fifth of one instrument cost. It is WITHHELD in both undegraded
# passes and was judged only at 07:44, where the degraded CPU inflated the absolute per-call cost
# past the resolve line -- so a degraded pass can also move a row INTO the gate's judgement. A row
# that thin must neither be added nor retired, which is what src/slow_calls.rs does: the
# instrument's own cost is bracketed per leg and checked against what this chip's recordings carry,
# and a row the measurement cannot resolve above that instrument is held in neither direction.
# THE COUNTED FORM OF THE GAP ABOVE, which no gate holds. The per-pipeline translation this header
# names is invisible to both halves: at 3.62x worst it is under the per-case margin, and a per-call
# row cannot carry it. In counts it is legible. Measured on this M3 Max over all 1103 cases, 8 runs
# of the whole selection at a one-minute load of 5.35, in the 539 cases that create a Metal pipeline
# state and carry a cost record:
#   Metal pipeline states created                       1,560
#   VkPipelines we made                                 2,634   = 1.69 each
#   of those, made at a state's creation                1,259
#     taken by a command                                  789
#     taken by none                                       470   = 37% of them
# So 1.69 VkPipelines per Metal pipeline state, 0.30 of them per state made for a command that never
# came. `variant_pipelines_made` is gated per case as an upper bound and `creation_pipelines_drawn`
# from below, but the RATIO is gated nowhere: a change that makes one more pipeline per state while
# the case grows a state passes both. That ratio is the per-pipeline translation expressed as a
# count, it needs no timing window, and it is the gate this cluster still wants.
# The largest single share of the 470 is the compute prediction missing because the dispatch names
# its own threadgroup size -- not a defect in the prediction, which a device test now pins as
# serving a dispatchThreads: over the predicted threadgroup (runtime tests::uniform_bind_offsets).
# The suite holds no dispatchThreadgroups: compute case, so the corpus cannot say how often an app
# hits it.
# WHY 1.69 AND NOT THE 2.56 THIS HEADER ONCE IMPLIED, stated so nobody reads a fix as a measurement
# artefact: integer-vertex-attributes reads 64 states, 64 predicted, 64 taken because the point-list
# prediction for an unrasterized state was FIXED (`Predict a point list for an unrasterized render
# state`, with `Census the mispredicted draws and bound the check's reach` beside it). Its earlier
# 64/0/128 was that bug, reproduced over three passes and gated at 128 as the blessed ceiling, not a
# loaded reading. The count fell because the waste went away.
# WHERE THE EXCESS SITS AFTER THE RE-RECORD, over 1,019 rankable rows at loads 3.79-8.61: Metal
# 25.56 s against our 8.64 s, ratio 0.338, with render_pipeline 38.3% of the excess and `wait`
# 28.2%. The two largest single rows are depth16-texel-reads at 160 ms and the extended-swizzles-*
# family at 43-97 ms each, the latter making 71 VkPipelines for 6 compute states with its
# dispatchThreads edge regions charged to `wait`. Both are open.
# So a row here needs a LOCALISED finding, not a pooled ratio: the first row below is 105x pooled
# and 1.2x over the three cases that obviously make it, and 265x over the 16 that actually do.
# Fields, tab-separated:
#   call                the Side call
# A COLD MEASUREMENT IS REPORTED AND NEVER JUDGED, so no row here is measured with
# `--cold-shaders`. That switch gives every case a fresh device as well as a fresh shader cache,
# and only on our leg, so a cold reading over the margin does not say whether the cost is our
# compile or first use on a new device: measured on this M3 Max, `target` is 0.9x warm and 14.3x
# cold and compiles nothing at all. Nine calls were over the margin cold against four warm, and
# seven of the nine were one mechanism. src/slow_calls.rs refuses to judge a cold run.
#   measured            the ratio its measurement read, with an x
#   where the cost is   the family it is in, and what the figure splits into
#   waiting on          what Metal does, what we do instead, and where the fix belongs
replace_region
column3: all of it in the 16 xr-two-plane-samples cases: one replaceRegion each, Metal 4 us against our 1210 us, 92% of ours blocked; the other 86 cases that make the call are 1.3x together
column4: Metal's replaceRegion on a two-plane extended-range texture answers in 4 us; ours waits about 1.1 ms, so we stage the upload and wait on it where Metal writes through. The fix is in the runtime's texture upload path for two-plane extended-range formats, not in the suite

column1: function_facts
column3: PER CASE WE ARE 25x FASTER: 0.04x over the 15 cases, Metal 343 ms against our 13 ms, because Metal compiles their AIR at `library` (21-24 ms a case) where we spend 0.05-0.25 ms. This row exists because the gate is per call, NOT because the call costs us anything against Metal. 15 calls over 15 cases, one each, Metal 216 us against our 10430 us, EVERY microsecond of ours our own CPU and nothing blocked. LOCALISED to the AIR decode: 14 of the 15 cases run 19.0x to 101.6x, and the one that does not is function-facts-visible at 0.2x -- a library's visible function, whose properties are a constant and need no decode. It is the only case of the family we are faster than Metal on. 40.6x in the other undegraded pass; the 89.5x on record elsewhere is the degraded pass and is not reproducible
column4: The suite's our_function_facts reads five MTLFunction property getters, and each recomputed the function's properties from scratch -- a full AIR decode, for the module-sourced functions newLibraryWithAIR makes -- so one call decoded one function's AIR five times, six with the constants dictionary, and ten for a specialized function, which decodes again to specialize. Metal answers every getter from the MTLFunction it already made. FIXED in metal2vulkan-runtime/src/library.rs, which now memoizes the properties on the function object as Metal holds them, and held by a count rather than a time (tests::derived_once, a table of getters each held to one derivation; with the memos bypassed its five rows read 10, 10, 2, 2 and 2). The constants dictionary named above is now memoized too, and the library's reflectionForFunctionWithName: with it. What the fix is proven by is the count, not a ratio: reading the getters computes the properties once where it computed them ten times, which is deterministic and needed no quiet host. The RATIO has not been re-measured and this row deliberately quotes no expectation for it, because the per-case figure above says the ratio was never a cost in the first place. Whoever re-measures should replace the 48.4x with what they read and leave the per-case line, which is the half that decides whether anything is wrong

column1: function_facts_from_descriptor
column3: PER CASE WE ARE 50x FASTER: 0.02x over the 7 cases, Metal 156 ms against our 3.8 ms, for the same reason as function_facts. The row is the gate's, not a cost. 7 calls over 7 cases, one each, Metal 94 us against our 3111 us, all of it our own CPU and nothing blocked; every one of the 7 is over the margin, 21.9x to 40.9x. 28.5x in the other undegraded pass; the 86.2x on record elsewhere is the degraded pass
column4: The same cause as function_facts and the same fix: newFunctionWithDescriptor: answers through the same our_function_facts, so it paid the same five-to-ten AIR decodes a call. Listed separately because the two calls are measured over different cases and a reader should not have to infer that one row covers both. Re-measurement is owed on the same terms as function_facts's

column1: render_pipeline
column3: THIS IS THE ONE ROW IN THIS FILE THAT CARRIES THE CLUSTER'S REAL COST, and the per-case breakdown of the two worst cases says so without ambiguity. integer-vertex-attributes is 3.62x a case: Metal 37.8 ms (library 23.5, render 7.6, 64 render_pipeline calls 1.7) against our 136.8 ms (64 render_pipeline calls 87.3, render 15.9, library 0.2, elsewhere 33.7), so render_pipeline is 85.6 ms of our 99 ms excess and 85.6 of our 103.1 ms in calls is our OWN CPU, not waiting. vertex-format-constant-step is 3.08x with the same shape (render_pipeline 71.2 ms of the excess). PER CASE over the blend sweeps 0.68x, two of them the wrong way (blend-sweep-write-masks 1.55x, blend-sweep-operations 1.25x) while carrying Metal's 27 ms library handicap. 660 calls over 120 cases, Metal 28606 us against our 886266 us, of which 831583 us is our own CPU. ATTRIBUTED, by the per-call cost against how many the case makes: Metal's marginal render pipeline gets cheap and ours does not. Metal costs a median 122.3 us a call in the 66 cases that make one, 31.0 us in the 11 that make 5 to 15 and 26.1 us in the 6 that make 36 or more -- it amortizes 4.7x. Ours costs 1686.0, 1277.5 and 1205.6 us over the same three groups, flat to within 1.4x. The ratio therefore climbs 13.8x, 41.3x, 46.1x with the call count while our own per-call cost barely moves, and on a case that makes ONE render pipeline we are faster than Metal (render-draw-forms-lines 0.4x). compute_pipeline is 0.4x at 26.2 us a call against Metal's 71.8, so this is the render path and not pipeline creation in general
column4: The cases that make many are the sweeps, which vary only pipeline state over one vertex-and-fragment pair (blend-sweep-*, vertex-format-*, integer-vertex-attributes; the blend slot sweeps need nothing of the fragment function). Metal compiles the functions once and makes cheap state variants; our per-call cost says we do the per-pipeline work again for each. What it is NOT is the shader compile: the measurement carried our shader cache over between the cases of a round, so the second and later pipelines of a sweep meet a warm cache and still cost about 1200 us each. For integer-vertex-attributes the translation is now fully accounted and NONE of it is redundant, so no cache is missing there: the case is 2 entry points x 16 attribute formats x 2 step functions, and shader_modules_made reads 34 = 2 + 32. Its 32 PerVertex pipelines share 2 modules, because an integer format read into a float attribute is fetched by fixed-function input in its USCALED/SSCALED form and vertex_fetch_projection's fetch_of drops the format for a fixed-function attribute, so the format never reaches the compile key. Its 32 Constant-step pipelines cannot be: Vulkan has no constant vertex input rate, so metal::vertex::fetch_as returns Pulled for that step, a pulled fetch reads bytes and converts in the shader, and the projection then carries the attribute and layout -- so the format IS in the key and each of the 16 needs its own vertex translation. 2 + 32 is the measured 34 exactly, and the step function being free while the format is not is why. The doubled predicted pipeline below was therefore the ONLY redundant work in this case. What this does NOT explain is the blend sweeps, which read shader_modules_made 2 over 32 pipelines and pipeline_layouts_made 1, so their cost is not translation at all but the per-pipeline work with a module already in hand, and that is where the remaining narrowing sits. THE NEXT NARROWING, identified and deliberately not built: blend-sweep-write-masks varies only the color write mask over one function pair, and VK_EXT_extended_dynamic_state3's COLOR_WRITE_MASK_EXT is wired but made dynamic only in a pipeline that reads through snapshots (pipeline/graphics.rs, GraphicsState::snapshot_reads), which these states do not, so 32 write-mask values become 32 VkPipelines where one dynamic pipeline would do. It is NOT proposed on this evidence, for a reason the venue gives: these figures come from MoltenVK, where Metal holds the write mask in MTLRenderPipelineState, so a dynamic write mask there buys a pipeline per bind instead of per creation and may cost more. Collapsing 32 makings to 1 is a claim about a driver with real dynamic state 3, and it needs a release-mode measurement on such a driver before anything is built. Recorded here so the next reader starts from the condition and not from the ratio. The contrast with compute_pipeline_bindings sharpens it: there our own cost falls 35x from the first pipeline on a shader to the eighth, so for compute the expensive part is once per shader; here it does not fall at all across 64, so for render it is once per pipeline. Whatever a render pipeline redoes, a compute pipeline keeps. ATTRIBUTED AND HALVED by that counters run. Every creation made a predicted VkPipeline the draw never took and the draw then made a second, so the per-pipeline work was done twice: integer-vertex-attributes read creation_pipelines_made 64, creation_pipelines_drawn 0, variant_pipelines_made 128, and vertex-format-float4 45/0/90. The cause is the creation-time prediction (pipeline/predicted.rs), which guessed a triangle list for an Unspecified topology class; these families discard rasterization and draw points, so the guess missed 100% of the time. Fixed: the counters now read 64/64/64 and 45/45/45, with shader_modules_made (34, 9) and pipeline_layouts_made (2, 2) unmoved, so SPIR-V and layouts were already shared and only the wasted pipeline changed. The deterministic check is the recorded bound and not a new test: variant_pipelines_made is gated at its reading with the case alone (cost.rs MONOTONE, where its largest alone over all 393 cases is recorded as 128 -- this case), and the committed recording for integer-vertex-attributes carries bounds creation_pipelines_made 64 against variant_pipelines_made 128, which is the doubling blessed as the ceiling. Re-blessing that bound to 64 fails a regression; the re-bless belongs on development and not in the change that earns it. WHAT REMAINS, and why this row keeps its figures: removing one of two pipelines per creation does not touch the flat per-call cost beneath it. Our cost per render pipeline is still flat to within 1.4x across 64 where Metal's falls 4.7x, so the amortization gap stands; about half of the 87.3 ms is expected to go and none of it is verified, because no window since has been judgeable. The blend sweeps that run the wrong way (write-masks 1.55x) make rasterizing states, read 32/32/32 before and after, and are NOT this cause. FOR THE OWNER: the cost half was not blind to this one, which is the lesson of the row -- it counted the second pipeline and recorded it as the bound, so a bound re-blessed from a measurement carries whatever waste the measurement had. The times half saw 3.62x on the case and judged nothing, because its margins are per call. THE CENSUS behind the fix, read offline from the committed recordings' own bounds and so load-independent: of the 356 cases that record making a predicted pipeline, 99 take every one, 206 never draw at all, and 51 mispredict a draw they do make, paying 121 pipelines twice. The 206 are NOT a defect -- a creation cannot know whether a draw will come, and paying the compile there is the point, since Metal pays it at library creation -- so the 121 are the whole of this bug and integer-vertex-attributes is 64 of them. A SECOND and distinct mispredict shape sits in the tail: 34 of the 51 are sample-positions-* and sample-fills-* cases wasting exactly 1 of 1, and GraphicsKey carries sample_positions and pass, neither of which a creation can know, so those cannot be predicted by a better guess at all; one pipeline a case, no per-case ratio, recorded here rather than fixed. THE CHECK'S REACH IS PARTIAL and this is the coverage finding: 398 of the 1099 recordings carry no cost recording whatever, among them vertex-format-float4, vertex-format-constant-step and every blend-sweep-*, which are exactly the many-pipeline cases with the worst per-case ratios. So a re-blessed bound holds integer-vertex-attributes and holds nothing for the other two cases this row quotes. Giving those cases a cost recording is what would extend it, and that write belongs on development with the re-bless. AGENTS.md gives pipeline-creation time its own ceiling rather than the device API's, so the row records the gap meanwhile

column1: compute_pipeline_bindings
column3: PER CASE WE ARE 6.5x FASTER: 0.15x over the 13 cases, Metal 320 ms against our 49 ms, every case between 0.01x and 0.32x, because Metal compiles their AIR at `library` (22-27 ms each) and we translate it here (1.0-6.9 ms). There is no cost gap to attribute. 13 calls over 13 cases, ONE call each, Metal 1755 us against our 41471 us, of which 40054 us is our own CPU: Metal a median 136.5 us a call against our 3004.8 us. 12 of the 13 cases are over the margin, 12.4x to 43.3x; the one that is not is function-bindings-argument-buffer at 0.3x. LOCALISED, by the one control the suite already contains: compute_pipeline_reflection_under makes the SAME runtime call (new_compute_pipeline_state_with_function_and_reflection) over the same three shader families and reads 0.7x -- because its cases make EIGHT each where these make one. On texture-slots, ours costs 1922 us for the one call here and 55 us a call over the eight there, while Metal costs 88 us and 29 us. OUR FIRST PIPELINE ON A SHADER COSTS ABOUT 1900-6900 us AND THE SECOND ONWARDS ABOUT 55 us; Metal's first costs 88-190 us. 21.7x in the other undegraded pass
column4: This is a first-use cost on a shader, not a per-pipeline one, and the 22x is what it looks like undiluted: each function-bindings-* case uses a different shader and makes exactly one pipeline, so each pays the whole of it, while compute_pipeline_reflection_under's cases spread the same cost over eight and it disappears. The 35x our own figure amortizes across those eight says the repeated part is small and the once-per-shader part is large. It is NOT the AIR-to-SPIR-V translation: the measurement carried our shader cache over between the cases of a round. The cost rises with the richness of the reflected arguments -- arrays 43.3x and array strides 31.4x at the top, imageblock 12.4x at the bottom, and an argument buffer, whose arguments we do not walk one by one, at 0.3x -- so the binding reflection over a function's data types is where to look. AGENTS.md gives pipeline-creation time its own ceiling rather than the device API's, so this row records the gap; attributing it needs the counters half over these 13 cases, which has not been run

column1: compute_pipeline_with_stage_input
column3: PER CASE THIS IS THE ONE THAT MOVES: attribute-format-* is 1.92x and attribute-format-fetches 2.68x (Metal 44.7 ms against our 119.6 ms), while attribute-stride-* is 0.07x. So of the pipeline rows this is the only family whose case total goes the wrong way, and attribute-format-fetches is the row to chase. 48 calls over 5 cases, Metal 1863 us against our 37152 us, all of it our own CPU. LOCALISED, and it is not the pipeline being expensive, it is the second one onwards: in the 3 cases that make ONE such pipeline we cost 41.4 us a call against Metal's 83.4 and are TWICE AS FAST (0.5x), and in the 2 cases that make 16 and 29 we cost 791.2 us a call against Metal's 34.5 (22.9x). Metal's marginal pipeline gets 2.4x cheaper with siblings in the case; OUR OWN per-call cost rises 19x. 22.6x in the other undegraded pass
column4: Our cost per pipeline growing with how many the case has already made is work that scales with the siblings, not with the pipeline, and a call that is cheaper than Metal's alone cannot be explained by pipeline creation being expensive. The two cases that make many are attribute-format sweeps over one kernel (attribute-format-fetches, attribute-format-class-crossings), so what varies between siblings is the stage-input descriptor alone. ANSWERED, and it is not the stride: measured on an M3 Max via MoltenVK, driving the cases' own descriptors through the runtime, attribute-format-fetches' 29 rows carry 29 distinct attribute-format tuples over ONE constant stride and make 29 shader modules with none shared -- one per row, irreducible, because the format is the decode -- while attribute-stride-* uses MTLBufferLayoutStrideDynamic, already the pushed form, and makes 1 module over 29 creations. Pool::has_room is ruled out too: the device's kept pools hold 3 blocks and 3 free ranges that never move over 400 creations. Nothing in WorkCounts rises over 410 creations and per-creation cost is flat across eight groups of 50. What remains is that each of this case's siblings is a cold shader where the one-pipeline cases hit a module the round already made: a cache-warmth difference between cases, not a structure that grows with the siblings

column3: PER CASE WE ARE 2.3x FASTER: 0.43x over the 2 cases, Metal 45.4 ms against our 19.4 ms. 16 calls over 2 cases, 8 each, Metal 962 us against our 19070 us, all of it our own CPU: 60.2 us a call against our 1191.9 us. Both cases are over the margin, 20.3x and 19.2x. 18.5x in the other undegraded pass
column4: Mesh pipeline creation with reflection, for an object-and-mesh stage pair. THE COUNTERS HALF IS BLIND TO THIS COST, which is the finding and the reason the row is not attributed. The case makes 8 states from ONE descriptor, varying only MTLPipelineOption -- the same shape as pipeline-options-texture-slots, where the 8 compute states cost 4 us each after the first and the counters read creation_pipelines_made 1, variant_pipelines_made 1, shader_modules_made 1. Here all 8 cost about 1390 us (median 1341 against a per-call mean of 1392, so none of them is a first-use outlier) and `cost --show` moves only 16 of the runtime's 471 counts, 4 of them in the translation region: shader_modules_made 4 with 28 shared and pipeline_layouts_made 1 with 7 shared, so modules and layouts ARE reused, and creation_pipelines_made and variant_pipelines_made do not move at all although their doc covers a render state's predicted key. ATTRIBUTED, and this row's own elimination of reflection was the error that hid it. The claim here was that reflection is cached on the PipelineKey and not the options, so the 8 states should share a key: true of the render path and false of the mesh path, which never built a key at all. The 8 shared nothing. Each state, and each read of a getter, did a full AIR decode of the object, mesh and fragment stages, reaching neither the shader cache nor any memo, while the drawing path went through the cache under render_descriptor_key -- so the 11.1 ms of wall that no counter accounted for was those decodes. Mesh reflection is now routed through the cache and memoized, and it is held by a count: tests::mesh_reflection_derived holds 2 states and 4 getter reads to 1 derivation, reads 0 with the routing removed, and a companion requires two different descriptors to derive 2 so the key cannot be too coarse. So the per-creation counter this row asked for is NOT owed: the cost is attributed and a derivation count holds it. The lesson the row keeps is that eliminating a cause by reading the path that caches it, rather than the path the case takes, eliminated the actual cause
